passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: You should read the following discussion of our financial condition and results of operations together with the consolidated financial statements and the notes to such statements included in this annual report. For the convenience of readers, NT dollar amounts used in this section for, and as of, the year ended December 31, 2025 have been translated into U.S. dollar amounts using US$1.00=NT$31.37, set forth in the statistical release of the Federal Reserve Board of the United States on December 31, 2025. The U.S. dollar translation appears in parentheses next to the relevant NT dollar amount. Overview A number of recent and expected future developments have had, and in the future may have, a material impact on our financial condition and results of operations. These developments include: • changes in our revenue composition and sources of revenue growth; • tariff adjustments; • capital expenditures as a result of technological advancements and changes in our business; • personnel expenses; and • taxation. Each of these developments is discussed below. Changes in our revenue composition and sources of revenue growth Our operating segments are (i) consumer business, (ii) enterprise business, (iii) international business and (iv) others. Operating segments are defined as components of an entity regarding which discrete financial information is available for regular evaluation of the chief operating decision maker, or decision-making group, in deciding how to allocate resources and in assessing performance. Our measure of operating segment performance is mainly based on revenues and income before income tax. credit_strengths.text: Chunghwa Telecom's consumer and enterprise segments generate stable, recurring revenue, with the enterprise ICT franchise expanding on IDC, cloud and cybersecurity demand. Operating margin sits above the Communication Services sector median, evidencing pricing power and cost discipline in a mature, capital-intensive market.

Internal cash generation is substantial: operating cash flow comfortably funds capital expenditure, leaving free cash flow that covers the disclosed dividend distribution. This self-funding profile, combined with a current ratio modestly above the sector median, supports liquidity without reliance on external borrowing.

key_risks.text: The debt note discloses only modest secured bank loans at the subsidiary level, with the unsecured facility fully repaid and the secured contract renewed to a medium-term maturity. Because no borrowing tags were reported at the balance-sheet date, total funded debt cannot be assembled, leaving leverage and refinancing metrics unverifiable.

MD&A flags tariff adjustments, shifting revenue composition, rising personnel expenses and taxation as material developments. Consumer voice revenue is declining and enterprise fixed-line revenue softened, so margin resilience depends on ICT growth offsetting legacy erosion; any tariff or cost shock would pressure the cash flow available for distributions.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is exceptionally high relative to the sector median, reflecting minimal gross interest expense against large operating income. Even if reported borrowings understate true funded debt, the earnings buffer is wide enough to absorb a material increase in interest cost without impairing debt service.

Free cash flow is strong and, after capital expenditure, exceeds the disclosed dividend distribution, indicating distributions are funded from internally generated cash rather than borrowings. This supports the view that debt service capacity is robust, though the absence of a complete debt figure prevents a precise coverage calculation.

overall_credit_view.text: Chunghwa Telecom presents a low-risk credit profile: dominant domestic telecom franchise, above-median operating margin, high interest coverage and self-funding cash flows. The indicative financial risk profile is unrated only because debt could not be assembled from standard tags, not because of evident weakness.

Our forward view is stable, assuming ICT revenue growth continues to offset legacy voice decline and capital spending remains within the disclosed run-rate. The material data gap is the missing debt balance, which prevents leverage and FCF-to-debt assessment; confirming borrowings, including leases, is a condition for final internal limits.

credit_strengths.text: 中華電信的消費者與企業業務板塊產生穩定、經常性收入，其中企業ICT業務因IDC、雲端及網路安全需求而擴張。營業利潤率高於通信服務行業中位數，證明其在成熟且資本密集的市場中具有定價能力與成本紀律。
內部現金生成能力雄厚：營運現金流足以輕鬆支應資本支出，留下可覆蓋已披露股利分派的自由現金流。此自我融資特性，加上流動比率略高於行業中位數，支持流動性而無需依賴外部借款。

key_risks.text: 債務附註僅披露子公司層面少量有擔保銀行貸款，無擔保融資額度已全額償還，有擔保合約已續約至中期到期日。由於資產負債表日未報告任何借款標籤，無法彙總總計息債務，致使槓桿及再融資指標無法驗證。
管理層討論與分析指出費率調整、收入結構變化、人事費用上升及稅務為重大發展。消費者語音收入正在下降，企業固網收入亦放緩，因此利潤率韌性取決於ICT增長能否抵銷傳統業務侵蝕；任何費率或成本衝擊都將對可用於分派的現金流構成壓力。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率相對於行業中位數極高，反映總利息費用極低而營業利潤龐大。即使報告借款低估了真實計息債務，盈利緩衝仍足夠寬廣，可吸收利息成本大幅上升而不損害債務償付。
自由現金流強勁，且在扣除資本支出後超過已披露股利分派，表明分派資金來自內部產生的現金而非借款。這支持債務償付能力穩健的觀點，儘管缺乏完整債務數據妨礙了精確的覆蓋率計算。

overall_credit_view.text: 中華電信呈現低風險信用狀況：國內電信主導地位、高於中位數的營業利潤率、高利息覆蓋率及自我融資的現金流。指示性財務風險狀況未評級僅因無法從標準標籤彙總債務，而非存在明顯弱點。
我們的前瞻觀點為穩定，假設ICT收入增長繼續抵銷傳統語音下滑，且資本支出維持在已披露的運行率內。重大數據缺口為缺失的債務餘額，這妨礙了槓桿及FCF對債務的評估；確認借款（包括租賃）是確定最終內部限額的條件。
